Bhupinder Singh & Ors. vs The State Of Delhi & Anr. on 20 July,
2023

 Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Dinesh Kumar Sharma
 Judgment
Dinesh Kumar Sharma, J. (Oral)
1.
The present petition has been filed seeking quashing of FIR No.0047 dated 08.02.2017 registered under Section 498A/406/34 IPC at PS Khyala, West.

2. FIR was lodged on the statement of 'Laxmi' wherein it has been submitted that the Respondent no.2/complainant married petitioner no.1 on 20.01.2016 at Tagore Garden, in accordance with the Hindu Rites and Ceremonies.
No child was born out of the said wedlock.

However, on account of temperamental differences and mental incompatibility, the parties started living separately as their relationship deteriorated since 11.07.2016 and instituted multiple litigations against each other and their respective families including the present FIR.
3. It has been also been stated that the petitioner No.1/Mr. Bhupinder Singh has expired on 05.02.2017.

4. Learned Counsel further submits that during the pendency of the proceedings, the parties have resolved their disputes amicably and in furtherance thereof they have entered into a settlement Bhupinder Singh & Ors. vs The State Of Delhi & Anr. on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85203918/
1 agreement dated 31.05.2022 before the Delhi Mediation Centre, Tis Hazari.

entities.text: Bhupinder Singh & Ors. vs The State Of Delhi & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the settlement it has been agreed between the parties that the petitioner shall pay Rs. 5,00,000/- in full and final settlement of the entire dispute to respondent no. 2/complainant.
5. It is submitted that during the course of the proceedings the petitioner No. 1 has already expired on 05.02.2017.
Therefore, the divorce could not take place as a result of the expiry of petitioner.

6. Furthermore, the Learned Counsel for the petitioners submits that since the parties have resolved all their differences amicably, therefore, it would be in the interest of justice to quash FIR No.0047 dated 08.02.2017 registered under Section 498A/406/34 IPC at PS Khyala, West all the proceedings emanating therefrom.
7. It is settled that the inherent powers under section 482 of the Code are required to be exercised to secure the ends of justice or to prevent abuse of the process of any court.
Further, the High Court can quash non- compoundable offences after considering the nature of the offence and the amicable settlement between the concerned parties.
Supreme Court and this Court have repeatedly held that the cases arising out of matrimonial differences should be put to a quietus if the parties have reached an amicable settlement.

Reliance may be placed upon: B.S. Joshi v. State of Haryana,
(2003) 4 SCC 675; K. Srinivas Rao v. D.A.Deepa, (2013) 5 SCC 226; Yashpal Chaudhrani and Others vs. State (Govt. of NCT Delhi) and Another, 2019 SCC OnLine Del 8179.
8.

sentences.text: Both parties are present in court and have duly been identified by the IO.
Respondent no. 2 submits that she has entered the settlement voluntarily without any fear, force or coercion.
She submits that other petitions have already been withdrawn or dismissed.

And since the petitioner has already expired and the settlement has already been taken place, respondent has no objection if FIR No.0047 dated 08.02.2017 registered under Section 498A/406/34 IPC at PS Khyala, West and all the proceedings emanating therefrom.
9. I have gone through the settlement which has been placed on record.

The matter has been amicably settled on the following terms and conditions:
1.

" That it is agreed between the parties that the parties have settle their present dispute for an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- as full and final settlement towards Istridhan, present past and future maintenance, jewellery articles etc. that alter the payment of the aforesaid amount, the complainant shall not claim regarding any movables or immovable articles/property of the respondents.

2. That it is also agreed between the parties that within a week from today complainant shall hand over the vacant possession of property bearing No.U-185,
Gali No.4, Shakarpur, Delhi-92 & shall also take her house hold articles from the said house.
At that time respondent shall hand over the copy of demand draft for an amount of Rs.2,00,000/-.

Bhupinder Singh & Ors. vs The State Of Delhi & Anr. on 20 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85203918/
2 3.

entities.text: Bhupinder Singh & Ors. vs The State Of Delhi & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That the compliance of above terms, the said demand draft for an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- in original shall be handed over by the respondents to the complainant before the concerned court.
4. That it is agreed between parties that after receiving the above said amount the complainant shall withdraw the present case which is pending before the Ld. Referral court.

5. That it is further agreed between the parties after withdrawing the Domestic violence case or any other cases criminal or civil in District or high court the respondents shall move appropriate petition in the Hon' ble High court of Delhi urging for quashing the present FIR No.47/2017, U/s 498A/406/34 IPC in view of the present settlement.

The respondents shall pay the final instalment of settlement amount of Rs.3,00,000/- (Rupees three Lakh only) to the complainant by way of cash(against receipt) DD/Pay Order/NEFT/RTGS/online mode in her favour.

The amount including all the pending arrears if any towards the complainant as direction of the Hon' ble court, the complainant has undertaken to co-operate in their said endeavor viz preparation of the petition, signing, swearing affidavits, appearing in the court and making statement etc.
6.

That on the aforesaid acts being done as stipulated, all disputes, differences between the parties shall stand settled and satisfied for all times to come and no claim whatsoever shall remain surviving against each other.
The parties undertake no to rake up or initiate any issue or claim before any court, forum or authority at any time in future.
7. That besides aforesaid cases mentioned herein above, if any other litigations dispute is found earlier or pending in the same would also be treated as settle/satisfied/ infructuous.

8. That the parties have gone though the terms and conditions hereinbefore recorded and have confirmed and verified the same to be correct and that they are going to sign it without any threat, pressure, coercion or undue influence from any quarter.

Both side undertake to abide by these terms and conditions."
10.

The remaining amount has been paid to respondent no.2 vide DD No. 496319 dated 26.04.2023 and the sum of Rs. 3 Lakh ( Rupees Three Lakhs) drawn on State Bank of India, Vikas Marg, Delhi in the name of Laxmi.

11. Taking into account the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, this court considers that the parties have entered into an amicable settlement out of their own free will, without any fear,
force or coercion and they should be given an opportunity to lead their lives peacefully.
No purpose will be served in continuing with the trial.

13. The present petition stands disposed of.
